primitives.name: Scan-Then-Lock
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Multiplicity.** How many hypotheses were actually examined before this one was singled out?
primitives.assumptions: Multiple hypothesis testing without proper correction; the specific effect was selected after examining the data.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Data Snooping Regime - where the apparent signal is an artifact of exploration rather than genuine discovery.

layer2.mapping: Bayesian posterior collapse under non-invariant priors; conformal prediction intervals fail to cover true parameters due to adaptive selection bias.
layer2.telemetry: Observed p-value distribution deviating from uniformity under the null hypothesis.

primitives.name: Acceptance Harness
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Standing laws you enforce - **No instrument's verdict counts** until that instrument has killed known-bad and passed known-planted-good at multiple n.
primitives.assumptions: The statistical tool has not undergone rigorous validation against both false positives (known-bad) and true positives (known-good).
primitives.breakdown_regime: Tool Reliability Degradation - when the instrument's outputs are unverified and potentially corrupted.

layer2.mapping: Algorithmic accountability through adversarial robustness testing; ensures that predictive models maintain valid uncertainty quantification.
layer2.telemetry: Failure rate of the instrument on synthetic benchmark datasets with known ground truth.

primitives.name: Statistical Power Bar
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **Statistical power bar (R62):** any new edge preregistration needs n >= 500, alpha = 0.05/33 family-corrected, frozen rules, prospective only.
primitives.assumptions: Minimum sample size of 500 to achieve adequate sensitivity; Bonferroni correction applied to control family-wise error rate across 33 tests.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Underpowered Detection - where small true effects are indistinguishable from noise due to insufficient data.

layer2.mapping: Minimum detectable effect size (MDES) calculation in A/B testing; requires pre-specified significance levels and effect sizes to avoid type-II errors.
layer2.telemetry: Observed statistical power (1 - \beta) below the desired threshold of 0.8 for the given effect size and sample size.

primitives.name: Hostile Statistical Referee
primitives.verbatim_quote: Not how many were reported -- how many were *looked at*.
primitives.assumptions: Results are derived from post-hoc examination of data, undermining the predictive validity of the claim.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Overfitting Catastrophe - where the model memorizes idiosyncratic noise rather than generalizable patterns.

layer2.mapping: Cross-validation as a surrogate for external validation; separates training and testing phases to prevent information leakage.
layer2.telemetry: Large discrepancy between in-sample fit metrics and out-of-sample performance metrics.

reasoning_traces.think:
The sovereign primitives formalize the core adversarial relationship between a claimant and a skeptical referee. The referee operates under a null hypothesis of "no edge," demanding that any positive result withstand systematic attacks. These include checking whether the instrument has been properly validated (Acceptance Harness), ensuring the study had sufficient power to detect the effect (Statistical Power Bar), verifying that the result was not found by searching through many possibilities (Multiplicity), and confirming that the analysis was prospective rather than a hindsight fit (Scan-Then-Lock). Together, they constitute a minimal set of requirements for credible evidence in high-stakes decision-making environments where prior failures have demonstrated the catastrophic cost of trusting unvetted algorithms.
